chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from one who narrated it, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:
Regarding dough that was kneaded and baked, then it became known that there was carrion in the water in it, he said: There is no harm; the fire has consumed what was in it.

key_terms.عُجِنَ: was kneaded or mixed into dough
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem or legal objection
key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: a dead animal or carrion causing impurity in context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on baked dough made with water later found to contain a dead animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about dough prepared with water later discovered to have been contaminated by a dead creature. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no problem in eating it after baking, because the fire consumed what was in it.
